summary: Self-hosted, community edition of Cal.com for scheduling meetings, with all enterprise code removed and an MIT licence.
whatItDoes: Cal.diy is a scheduling platform you run on your own server: people book time with you through your booking pages, and it connects to calendars and video tools. It is a fork of Cal.com with the commercial and enterprise code taken out.
problem: Hosted scheduling tools like Calendly keep your calendar data on their servers. Cal.diy lets individuals and self-hosters run their own scheduling without a licence key or a Cal.com account.
whoFor: Individuals who want a self-hosted Calendly alternative
Self-hosters comfortable running a server and database
Developers who want an MIT-licensed scheduling codebase
whyChoose: It is 100% MIT-licensed with no license key required and no proprietary Enterprise Edition features.
requirements: Or Docker and docker compose for the Docker setup
overview: Cal.diy is the community-driven, open-source scheduling platform: a fork of Cal.com with all enterprise and commercial code removed. Everything works without a Cal.com account or licence.

The README is clear that it is meant for personal, non-production use, and that self-hosting needs real knowledge of server administration, databases and securing sensitive data. For commercial use, the project points you to Cal.com.

Compared with Cal.com, Teams, Organizations, Insights, Workflows, SSO/SAML and other enterprise features are removed. Integrations such as Google Calendar, Microsoft Graph, Zoom, Daily and HubSpot can be set up with your own credentials.

steps.title: Generate NEXTAUTH_SECRET
steps.body: Put the output in NEXTAUTH_SECRET in .env. Using the default placeholder in production is a security risk.

steps.title: Generate CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY
steps.body: Put the output in CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY in .env.

steps.title: Start Cal.diy
steps.body: This runs a local Postgres database, the Cal.diy web app and Prisma Studio.

steps.title: Clone and enter the folder
steps.body: On Windows, the README says to clone with core.symlinks=true in Git Bash with admin rights.

steps.title: Set up .env
steps.body: Duplicate .env.example to .env and add NEXTAUTH_SECRET and CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY as above.

steps.title: Quick start
steps.body: Needs Docker. Starts a local Postgres with test users; the credentials are logged in the console.

environment.name: NEXTAUTH_SECRET
environment.description: Cookie encryption key. Generate with openssl rand -base64 32.

environment.name: CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY
environment.description: Authentication encryption key (32 bytes for AES256). Generate with openssl rand -base64 24.

firstRun.title: Finish the setup wizard
firstRun.body: Open http://localhost:3000. The first time you run Cal.diy, a setup wizard asks you to define your first user.

tutorial.title: Set up your own booking page
tutorial.useCase: You want people to book meetings with you on a scheduler you host.

steps.title: Skip the calendar step if you like
steps.body: If the setup wizard's Connect your Calendar step blocks you, go straight to <NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL>/event-types. You can add calendars later under Settings > Integrations.

steps.title: Create an event type
steps.body: Add an event type for the kind of meeting people can book.

steps.title: Connect a calendar
steps.body: Add Google Calendar with your own Google API credentials, as the integrations section describes.

steps.title: Share the link
steps.body: Send your booking link to the people who need to book time with you.

tutorial.expected: A booking page on your own server where people can pick a time with you.

costs.label: Hosting
costs.value: There is no hosted version, so you pay for your own server and database.

troubleshooting.solution: Generate web push keys with npx web-push generate-vapid-keys and set NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY and VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY in .env.
Set NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000/api/auth so the backend can loop back to itself.

troubleshooting.problem: Requests are rejected behind a load balancer that handles SSL
troubleshooting.solution: The README suggests NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, but only if you trust the services directing traffic to your server.
